REPORT 
 
PART-I 
 
I.  INTRODUCTORY 
 
1.1  Indian Railways continues to serve as the backbone of the nation’s 
transportation system, connecting diverse regions and driving economic growth 
through its extensive and integrated network. Reflecting the Government’s sustained 
commitment to infrastructure expansion and modernization, the Capital Outlay for 
2026–27 has been pegged at Rs. 2,93,030 crore, which is Rs. 27,830 crore higher than 
the Revised Estimates for 2025 –26. The Gross Budgetary Support (GBS) has been 
fixed at Rs. 2,78,030 crore, supplemented by Rs. 3,000 crore from Internal Resources 
and Rs. 12,000 crore under Extra Budgetary Resources (Partnership).  
1.2 The Annual Plan for 2026 –27 places continued emphasis on removal of traffic 
bottlenecks, capacity augmentation and strengthening of safety infrastructure across 
the railway network. In pursuit of these objectives, substantial allocations have been 
made under Budgetary Sources in BE 2026 –27, including Rs. 36,722 crore for New 
Lines, Rs. 37,750 crore for Doubling works, Rs. 22,853 crore for Track Renewals, Rs. 
800 crore for Safety Works at Level Crossings, Rs. 8,225 crore for Road Over/Under 
Bridges (ROBs/RUBs) and Rs. 7,500 crore for Signal and Telecommunication works.  
The overall Capex allocated for capacity augmentation stands at Rs.1,13,670 crore, for 
customer amenities at Rs. 11,900 crore and for rolling stock and inventories at Rs. 
64,397 crore. 
1.3 Indian Railways have formulated the National Rail Plan (NRP) with the 
objective of creating a “future -ready” railway system by infrastructure augmentation. 
The Plan envisions meeting the growing demand for passenger and freight transport, 
segregating freight and passenger traffic on High Density Networks through 
Dedicated Freight Corridors, enhancing speeds of both freight and passenger trains, 
expanding connectivity to ports, mines and industrial clusters, and increasing the

1.4 Indian Railways have completed several landmark railway infrastructure

Udhampur–Srinagar–Baramulla Rail Link (272 km) has been dedicated to the nation,

first vertical lift sea bridge connecting Rameswaram Island to the mainland, marks a

3.3 The main objectives and thrust areas of Annual Plan 2026 -27 are expanding, 
modernizing and enhancing the operational efficiency of the railway. The Ministry 
while detailing the main objectives and thrust areas remarked as under: 
 
A. Capacity Augmentation and Network Expansion: 
• New Lines (PH11) :  Construction of new rail lines presents a strategic 
avenue for enhancing last -mile connectivity. It contributes significantly 

7 
 
to economic development, particularly in remote areas, such as the 
Northeastern states and Jammu & Kashmir, Himachal Pradesh and 
Uttarakhand. New rail lines are planned to make travel easier within the 
country, helping people reach and leave areas that are difficult to 
access. Construction of new railway lines helps reduce congestion on 
existing routes by providing additional capacity for passenger and 
freight services. Improved transportation infrastructure attracts 
investment, support tourism, and enhance regional development. It also 
provides environmental benefits such as reduction of greenhouse gas 
emissions and contributes to a more sustainable and green 
transportation system by providing an alternative to road transportation. 
• Gauge Conversion (PH14)  :  Gauge conversion projects provide a 
uniform gauge for the smooth and fast flow of traffic, which is 
necessary for strategic and operating point of view. It improves the 
operational efficiency. 
• Doubling (PH15) :  The plan prioritizes the expansion of rail network 
capacity to meet the increasing demand for passenger and freight 
services. Projects for track doubling, tripling, and even quadrupling are 
underway to enhance line capacity. 
• Double-track railways use each track exclusively in one direction. This 
arrangement simplifies signaling systems. When one track of a double -
track railway is out of service due to track maintenance work or a train 
breaks down or during an unusual (Accident or ACF), all trains may be 
concentrated on a single usable track.  Maintenance 
and engineering work are easier on tracks in quadruple line with little 
resulting delay because standard double-track service can continue even 
if the other two double tracks are halted during the work. 
• Traffic Facilities (PH16) – Yard remodeling helps reduce congestion 
and improve the movement of passenger and freight trains. It involves 
interlocking of tracks to increase safety and capacity. Old yards were 
built for past needs, so remodeling removes issues like short shunting 

8 
 
necks and inadequate lines for cleaning or stabling trains. It also 
allows for more platforms to handle more trains, improving efficiency 
and reducing delays. Overall, yard remodeling is essential for 
improving railway infrastructure and making train services more 
reliable and efficient. 
• Dedicated Freight Corridors (PH61)  - Completion and 
operationalization of key sections of the Western Dedicated Freight 
Corridors to decongest the existing network. 
B. Modernization and Technological Upgradation: 
• Computerization (PH17)  : Updating mobile app services for 
passengers to improve the booking process and offer real -time train 
tracking.  Freight digitalization by online Indent placement, Supply 
information, Freight calculation and payment, Movement of receipt, 
Tracking of consignment, Detention charges (wharfage, demurrage) 
application. 
• Rolling Stock (PH21)  – Operationalization of coaches like; Vande 
Bharat, Amrit Bharat, LHB and Vande Sleeper, equipped with GPS, 
Wi-Fi, bio -toilets, and real -time information systems and upgraded 
interiors for enhancing passenger services. Acquisition of modern 
locomotives, exemplified by the WAG -12, represents a remarkable 
advancement in terms of power output and capabilities. Introduction of 
modern age wagons like Flat Multi -purpose Wagon, BCATIC and 
BLSS. 
• S&T Works (PH33)  - Advance signaling technologies such as 
Automatic Block Signaling (ABS) for  increased train frequency , 
KAVACH to avoid train collision etc. are useful in improving safety 
and efficiency. 
• Customer Amenities (PH53)  - Station Modernization by 
redevelopment of major railway stations under Amrit Bharat Station 
Scheme to provide world -class facilities to passengers. Modern Goods 

9 
 
Shed with high level platform, cover over platform, lighting and 
concrete pathways. 
• National High -Speed Rail Corporation Limited (PH61)  – Notable 
progress on Mumbai-Ahmedabad bullet train project. 
C. Safety and Security: 
• Road Safety Works - LC/ROB/RUB (PH29/30) - Continuing efforts to 
eliminate all unmanned level crossings across the broad -gauge network. 
The closure of level crossings and the construction of Road Over 
Bridges (ROBs) or Road Under Bridges (RUBs) offer numerous 
benefits, contributing to enhanced safety, efficiency, and overall 
effectiveness of railway and road transportation systems. 
• Track Renewal/Bridge Works, Tunnel Works & Approaches  (PH31/32) 
- Significant investments in renewing old tracks, bridges and tunnels to 
enhance safety, Capacity, Operational Efficiency, Long -Term 
Durability and Passenger Experience. 
• Workshops including Production Units (PH42) – Workshops and PUs 
contribute to the overall performance of the rail network by facilitating 
timely repairs, maintenance, and production of rolling stocks. This, in 
turn, enhances the reliability and efficiency of the railway system, 
fulfils operational needs, enhance safety standards, and boost capacity 
and throughput. 
D. Electrification: 
• Electrification Projects (PH35) - Indian Railways aims to achieve 100% 
electrification. This is in line with the goal of reducing dependence on 
fossil fuels and making railways a greener, more sustainable mode of 
transportation. 
E. Sustainability and Green Initiatives: 
• Other Specified Works (PH64) - Projects include installation of solar 
power plants, rainwater harvesting systems and water recycling plants at 
stations and maintenance depots. 
F. Human Resource Development: 

10 
 
• Training/HRD (PH65) - Training programs to equip railway personnel with 
up-to-date skills and knowledge, preparing them to handle the complexities 
of modern railway operations. It leads to a more competent and efficient 
workforce to insure safety and operational efficiency. 
G. Urban Transport Integration: 
• Metropolitans Transport Project (PH81) - Expanding and improving 
suburban rail networks in major metropolitan areas to ease congestion and 
provide better connectivity for commuters. 
H. Freight Sector Development: 
• Encouraging public -private partnerships (PPPs) in freight operations, 
development of private freight terminals, and wagon leasing. 
I. Financial Sustainability and Resource Mobilization: 
• Monetization of Assets: Indian Railways plans to monetize assets like land, 
stations, and other infrastructure through long -term leasing and 
partnerships with private players. 
• Non-Fare Revenue: Increasing non -fare revenue through advertising, real 
estate development, and leasing of railway infrastructure.

IV. INTERNAL RESOURCES  
 
4.1 The Ministry while commenting on static year on year trend of Internal 
Resources detailed the action plan to meet the target of RE during the remaining 
period of 2025 -26 and concrete initiatives taken to increase the internal resources of 
the Railways as under :- 
• “Indian Railways incurred revenue expenditure of ₹ 2,63,018 crore in 
2024–25, with nearly 90% classified as inelastic and committed 
expenditure, increasing annually which includes establishment cost, 
pension, lease, fuel charges etc. 
• Passenger services are highly subsidized, with an average concession of 
about 45%, and uneconomical routes are operated to maintain connectivity 
to remote and rural regions. 
• As a result, Indian Railways bears a social service obligation exceeding ₹ 
40,000 crore annually. 
• The expenditure is increasing year on year on account of: 
o Periodic increases in pay and allowances 
o Fresh recruitments 
o Higher maintenance costs due to addition of new assets 
o Repayment of the COVID -related loan from the Ministry of Finance 
(MoF) 
• Despite substantial fixed and rising obligations, Indian Railways 
consistently generates operational surplus through: 
o Strong freight performance 
o Improved asset utilization 
o Cost rationalization 
• Since 2022 –23, Railways has undertaken record levels of capital 
expenditure (capex) focused on: 
o New lines 
o Track doubling 

13 
 
o Electrification 
o Rolling stock expansion 
o Modern signaling systems 
These investments are long-term growth enablers, not merely expenditures. 
• Over time, enhanced capacity and efficiency from this capex are expected 
to result in: 
o Higher freight and passenger revenues 
o Improved logistics competitiveness 
o Reduced logistics costs 
o Stronger export competitiveness 
o Greater support to the national economy 
Measures to improve Internal Resources: 
   In RE 2024 -25, Railways targeted to achieve internal resource of Rs. 
2,141 cr. and against this Railway achieved Rs. 3,460 cr. internal resources. To 
increase internal resources, IR have to increase Railways’ earnings and control 
expenditure. Therefore, to increase revenue, several measures have been taken by 
Indian Railways. These include the following: 
• To increase the network capacity, rail network expansion has been taken up in 
a big way by construction of new lines, multi tracking of existing lines and 
gauge conversion of existing lines.  
▪ Removing bottlenecks in operations by yard remodeling, construction of 
bypass/chord lines, rail flyovers etc. 
▪ The construction of Eastern Dedicated Freight Corridor (EDFC) from Ludhiana 
to Sonnagar (1,337 Km) and Western Dedicated Freight Corridor (WDFC) 
from Jawaharlal Nehru Port Terminal (JNPT) to Dadri (1,506 Km) has 
completed apporx. 96% as out of total 2,843 kms, 2,741 route kms (96.4%) 
has been commissioned and operational. Remaining 102 Km of WDFC will be 
completed by May,2026. 
▪ Indian Railways has taken up electrification of Railway lines in a mission 

14 
 
mode. So far, about 99.1% of Broad Gauge (BG) network has been electrified.  
▪  Procurement of Wagons and Locomotives: To increase freight carrying 
capacity, large numbers of IR wagons have been procured and locomotives 
have been manufactured. During 2014 to 2025, about 2 lakh wagons have 
been procured and more than 10,000 locomotives have been added for 
increasing freight loading and mobility. 
▪  Industry participation in investment in General Purpose Wagons, Special 
Purpose/High- Capacity wagons and Automobile carrier wagons for cement, 
oil, steel, fly-ash, automobile etc. So far, around 240 rakes of special purpose 
wagons, 374 rakes of general -purpose, wagons and 48 rakes of automobile 
wagons have been inducted. 
▪  Under the ‘Gati Shakti Multi-Modal Cargo Terminal (GCT)’ policy so far, 124 
terminals completed, 290 are in process, with an estimated traffic capacity of 
192 million tonnes per annum (MTPA).  
▪ A “Bulk Cement Terminal Policy” for setting up terminals on Railway land has 
been launched recently as part of Railway reforms for facilitating Bulk 
Cement transportation. 
▪ Ensuring increased availability of rakes/wagons against demand. 
▪ Use of Information Technology in freight operations to improve monitoring 
and utilization of assets. 
▪ Induction of higher horsepower locomotives. 
▪ Improvement in maintenance practices of wagons and locomotives resulting in 
increased availability of loco and rolling stock for traffic use. 
▪ Improvement in track and signaling standards to carry higher volume of traffic. 
 Because of the above measures, the cargo loading has increased from 1,052 MT in 
2013-14 to 1,615 MT in 2024 -25 i.e. increase of about 54%. The total traffic 
revenue has also increased substantially during this period from Rs. 1,39,838 cr. in 
2013-14 to Rs. 2,65,004 cr. in 2024-25 i.e. increase of about 90%.  
To enhance passenger revenue, passenger fare has been increased in certain 
classes. Railways are also running special trains during Diwali, Chhath, Holi, 

15 
 
Summer and Holiday season. The other initiatives have also been undertaken to 
enhance sundry earnings as given below: 
• Station Seva and Suvidha at Amrit Bharat Stations Anubandh: This 
initiative, One Station- One Service Provider, could be a key contributor to 
increasing NFR through enhanced services and infrastructure utilization 
• Yatri Seva Anubandh  (YSA) - One train - One Service Provider: To 
provide seamless service to the passengers. This eliminates fragmented 
contracts and enhances earnings. 
• Rail Display Network (RDN): To disseminate railway information and 
generate revenue through digital advertising across the railway network. 
• Gaming and Recreation Zones: The proposed gaming and recreation zones, 
in collaboration with RailTel, could yield higher revenues. 
• Branding of Summer and Winter Special Trains: Seasonal branding and 
partnerships can provide new revenue opportunities through advertising 
and sponsorship deals. 
Moreover, to enhance revenue by fully utilizing the extensive advertisement space, 
the existing policies of NINFRIS (New and Innovative Non -Fare Revenue Ideas 
Scheme), ATMs, and the other policies are suitably being modified and on 
boarded with the e-auction policy and to align with the Out of home(OOH) market 
conditions. Railways realized a Sundry earning of Rs. 3,129 cr. from Land in 
2024-25 alone. By implementing these initiatives, Indian Railways may 
significantly enhance its sundry earnings and increase its share to Railways total 
receipts. 
Further, Railway is also taking various steps to optimize revenue expenditure as 
given below:- 
• Rigorous monitoring of expenditure w.r.t. the monthly budget proportions 
based on Spending Limits.  
• Implementation of the guidelines on expenditure control & management 
circulated by the Ministry of Finance on the Railways also. 

16 
 
• Optimizing expenditure in areas such as contractual payment, overtime 
allowance, purchase of material etc. 
• Progressive electrification and reduction in expenditure under HSD oil, 
optimizing the fuel consumption, Energy Audit, etc. 
• Improvement in inventory management 
• Prioritization of expenditure on works for better use of available resources. 
• Better asset utilization. 
• Improving staff productivity by better man-power planning. 
Due to progressive electrification of Railway tracks more than Rs. 8,000 cr. (Rs. 
4,700 cr. in 2023-24 and Rs. 3,300 cr.  in 2024 -25) has been saved in last two year 
under Diesel traction. 
As a result of all these ongoing measures, Railways generated a Net Revenue of 
Rs. 2,660 against target of Rs. 1,341 cr. in 2024-25.”

During preparation of the DPR, due care is taken to ensure that no delays occur 
on account of level crossings. Elimination of level crossings (LCs) is a 
continuous and dynamic process of Indian Railway. Such works are taken up 
on the basis of its impact on safety in train operations, mobility of trains & 
impact for road users and feasibility etc. LCs are eliminated either by providing 
ROBs/ RUBs in lieu of LCs or through direct closure (for low traffic LCs) or 
by diversion of road traffic to nearby ROB/RUB/LC depending upon the site 
conditions. 
Completion of Railway project/s depends on various factors which include the 
following:  
• Land acquisition by State Government 
• Forest clearance 
• Shifting of infringing utilities 
• Statutory clearances from various authorities 
• Geological and topographical conditions of area

Modernization and Improvement/up -gradation of Rolling Stock to enhance 
safety, convenience and comfort of passengers is a continuous and ongoing 
process on Indian Railways. 
The following new technologies have been adopted in locomotives in recent 
years:  
i) Head on Generation Technology: In HOG system electrical power is 
fed to the coaches directly from the Overhead Equipment (OHE) through 
the Locomotive. It eliminates the need for separate diesel fuelled power 
cars in trains and thus reduces the need for pulling extra coaches and also 
increases efficiency further resulting in reduction in carbon footprint.  
Indian Railways have a total of 2342 HOG compliant locomotives as in 
January 2026. 
ii) Provision of RMS on electric locos: Remote Monitoring System helps in 
remote diagnostic of the failures in the locomotives bringing down the 
failure investigation time. As in January 2026, it has been commissioned 
on about 2233 electric locomotives and 2910 diesel locomotives. 
iii) Kavach (loco equipment): Kavach is an indigenously developed Automatic 
Train Protection (ATP) system. Kavach aids the loco pilot in train running 
within specified speed limits by automatic application of brakes in case it is 
exceeded to ensure safely. 
iv)  High Reach Pantographs: High Reach Pantographs are being provided to 
for seamless working in high -rise OHE territory. Till date, 5655 
locomotives have been provided with High Reach Pantographs 
pantographs. 
v) Waterless urinals: Waterless Urinals are being provided in locomotives as 
an amenity to the loco crew.  These are robust in design considering riding 
shocks and vibrations and can be retrofitted without many alterations to 
layout and without interference with working of other equipment of 
locomotive.  Till date more than 2000 locomotives have been provided 
with Urinals as in January 2026. 

44 
 
vi) LED headlight:   LED Headlights are being provided in locomotives to 
improve visibility to Loco Pilots during train operations.  7362 locomotives 
have been provided with LED Headlights. All new locomotives are being 
manufactured with LED Headlights.  Total 8718 locomotives are provided 
with LED Headlights as in January 2026.   
vii) Energy saving mode in electric locomotives:   To save Electrical Energy in 
3-phase freight locomotives (WAG9/WAG9H/WAG9HC) modification is 
being carried out in existing scheme of load distribution and ‘Energy 
Saving Mode’ has been included in software of Auxiliary converter to put 
off the auxiliary blowers of locomotives, when cooling is not required 
during the idling of locomotives.  3028 locomotives have been modified 
with this feature as in January 2026. 
Technological improvement is a continuous process. As a step towards the 
modernization of Indian Railways (IR), many technology driven projects are 
being introduced to improve upon the Safety & Productivity and to enhance 
availability, reliability, operability, maintainability of the Rolling Assets like 
Wheel Impact Load Detector (WILD) and Hot Axlebox Hot Wheel (HAHW) 
Detector/Hot Box Detector (HBD). WILD is a way -side inspection system that 
measures the impact of wheel on tracks to automatically identify the defective 
wheels in Rolling Stock and HAHW/HBD are automatic systems consisting of 
infrared sensors installed on wayside to measure the temperature of axle 
bearing box/wheel of rolling stock while in motion. 
Further, as a step towards inducting latest technology on IR, the pilot projects 
viz. Machine Vision based Inspection Systems (MVIS) and Automatic Wheel 
Profile Measurement System (AWPMS) have been taken up. The MVIS will 
generate alerts on detecting any hanging, loose or missing components of 
moving trains and AWPMS allows automatic non-contact measurement of train 
wheel profile ensuring measurement of wheel geometry and wear. 
In addition, installation of CCTV cameras in coaches and locomotives has been 
taken up to strengthen passenger security. 

45 
 
Innovation is a continuous process to Rolling Stock Manufacturing to enhance 
safety, convenience and passenger comfort. All the Production units of Indian 
Railways are International Railway Industry Standard  (IRIS) certified units 
adopting International Standards and practices in Rolling Stock manufacture. 
RDSO, the research, design and standardization organization regularly

Further, development / upgradation of railway stations is complex in nature 
involving safety of passengers & trains and requires various statutory 
clearances such as fire clearance, heritage, tree cutting, airport clearance etc. 
The progress also gets affected due to brownfield related challenges such as 
shifting of utilities (involving water/sewage lines, optical fibre cables, gas pipe 
lines, power/signal cables, etc.), infringements, operation of trains without 
hindering passenger movement, speed restrictions due to works carried out in 
close proximity of tracks and high voltage power lines, etc. and these factors 
affect the completion time. 
Development/Upgradation/Modernisation of stations including under Amrit 
Bharat Station Scheme is generally funded under Plan Head -53 ‘Customer 
Amenities’. The details of allocation and expenditure under Plan Head -53 are 
maintained Zonal Railway -wise and not work -wise or station wise or state -
wise. The fund allocation of ₹ 12,120 crore has been made for the financial 
year 2025-26 under Plan Head –53 and expenditure (up to December, 2025) of 
₹ 9,660 crore has been incurred so far.” 
12.2 The following mechanisms and monitoring systems have been put in place by 
the Ministry to ensure timely execution of station redevelopment projects and to 
prevent cost overruns and delays: 
“Indian Railways has a well-established mechanism to monitor implementation 
of projects including their reviews, inspection, check for time and cost 
overruns, quality of works and audits. Monitoring of projects is done at various 

52 
 
levels including through dedicated portal of Indian Railways named Indian 
Railway Project Sanction and Management (IRPSM). Works are carried out 
adhering to the standards and specifications laid down in various codes and 
manuals. Inspections/audits/checks are carried out from time to time by various 
agencies/officials/multi-disciplinary teams as per laid down instructions and 
actions for correction are taken immediately. The issues faced by the executing 
units are accordingly addressed. This is a continuous and ongoing process.” 
12.3 The Ministry provided the following details of railway stations redeveloped or 
proposed to be redeveloped under the Public Private Partnership (PPP) model and the 
mechanism for dissemination of key lessons and best practices deriving from station 
redevelopment initiatives undertaken under the PPP model : 
“Ministry of Railways explored various models of development of stations 
including Public Private Partnership (PPP). Rani Kamalapati station in the state 
of Madhya Pradesh has already been developed and commissioned under PPP 
model. Presently, 15 nos. of stations namely Avadi, Andheri, Anand Vihar, 
Bhopal, Bangalore City, Chennai Central, Coimbatore Jn.,   Dadar, Delhi 
junction, Hazrat Nizamuddin, Tambaram, Kalyan, Pune, Vadodara and 
Vijayawada have been identified for development on PPP model. Out of these 
15 stations identified under PPP mode, the proposal for redevelopment of 
Vijayawada Railway Station has been approved by the competent authority on 
PPP (Design, Build, Finance, Operate and Transfer) mode and the bid has been 
invited for the project. The other 14 stations have been taken up for Master 
planning and financial modelling. 
Public Private partnerships have evolved over time and experience gained from 
the redevelopment of Rani Kamalapati station on PPP mode provides important 
lessons for designing sustainable PPP frameworks. In comparison to earlier 
PPP models of station redevelopment, the revised model incorporates a more 
balanced risk -sharing approach, greater contractual clarity and enhanced 
commercial flexibility. These measures are expected to improve bankability of 
the project, reduce uncertainty for private participants and increase investor 

53 
 
confidence in station redevelopment projects under the PPP framework. The 
provisions to ensure equitable allocation of risks by distinguishing between 
delays attributable to the Authority and those attributable to the 
Concessionaire, have been incorporated thereby providing contractual certainty 
and reducing exposure to unforeseen delays.”

Further, Indian Railways is committed to make its railway stations accessible 
for Persons with Disabilities (Divyangjans) and passengers with reduced 
mobility as part of “ सुगम्य भारत  अभभयान ” or ‘Accessible India Campaign’ of 
Government of India. In compliance of the Rights of Persons with Disabilities 
Act, 2016, “Guidelines on accessibility of Indian Railway stations and facilities 
at stations for differently abled persons (Divyangjans) and passengers with 
reduced mobility” have been circulated and notified in the Gazette of India.

The guidelines include provisions of facilities for Divyangjans and passengers 
with reduced mobility such as entrance ramps, accessible parking, low height 
ticket counters/help booths, toilets, drinking water booths, subways/foot over

tactile pathways for visual impairment, etc. which are being provided in a 
phased manner and on the principles of reasonable accommodation. 
Standardisation and upgradation of drawings and designs is a continuous and 
ongoing process based on past experience, extant codal provisions,

13.2 The following steps as detailed by the Ministry are being taken to improve 
capacity and cost efficiency of rail freight operations and to raise the maximum speed 
of freight trains to 100 kmph : 
“DFCCIL has significantly enhanced the efficiency of freight transportation, 
resulting in faster movement of traffic from industrial hubs to ports and from 
coal mines to thermal power plants. This has led to minimizing transit delays, 
lowering inventory holding requirements, and reducing wastage and 
degradation of goods during transit. 
● Trucks on Train (ToT): Enables loaded trucks to be transported on flat rail 
wagons, reducing transit time, road congestion, and carbon emissions. 
● Double stack container trains: Enhancing containerization efficiency for 
higher cargo capacity and reduced freight by 50% for upper deck. 
● Simplified Business Processes: IT -driven solutions for ease of doing 
business 
      Steps to improve the average speeds 
● Segregation of wagons to optimize the maximum permissible speeds of 
rakes 
● Induction of 100 kmph speed potential wagons  
● Indian Railway’s Terminals capacity enhancements to reduce bottlenecks 
at exit points of DFC 
● more holding lines on EDFC & WDFC 

60 
 
●   Centralized traffic control (CTC) system over DFC Introduction of 
Kavach. 
To improve the efficiency of rail freight handling at the terminals, Indian 
Railway has adopted two - pronged approach: encouraging private sector 
to develop the modern rail freight terminals and augmenting/ upgrading 
the infrastructure at railway owned goods sheds.  GCT policy provides 
framework for development of rail freight terminals equipped with 
modern facilities including mechanized handling. Till date, a total of 124 
GCTs have already been commissioned. Further, a work of Rs.14,500 
crore has been sanctioned for development of customer amenities at the 
goods sheds and parcel offices during 2023-24, 2024-25 & 2025-26.”

XIV. UPGRADATION OF TRACKS AND SIGNALLING SYSTEMS IN 
INDIAN RAILWAYS 
 
14.1 Strengthening, upgradation, modernisation  and improvement of track 
infrastructure is a continuous and ongoing process over Indian Railways. The 
following measures as detailed by the Ministry are being taken by Indian Railways to 
upgrade railway tracks:  
i. Modern track structure consisting of 60kg, 90 Ultimate Tensile Strength (UTS) 
rails, Wider and heavier Pre -stressed Concrete Sleepers (PSC) with elastic 
fastening, fan -shaped layout turnout on PSC sleepers and H -beam Sleepers on 
girder bridges are being used while carrying out primary track renewals.  
ii. The Thick Web Switches and Weldable CMS Crossings are being used in 
turnout renewal works.  
iii. Supply of 260m long rail panels have been increased to avoid welding of joints, 
thereby improving safety and riding quality  
iv. Thick Web Switch Expansion Joints are being used in place of earlier 
Conventional/Improved SEJs. 
v. Adoption of better welding technology for rails i.e. Flash Butt Welding.  
vi. Adoption of mechanized system for track maintenance using high output plain 
tampers and points & crossing tampers for improved maintainability & 
reliability of track.   
vii. Deployment of state -of-the-art modern machines including Rail Grinding 
Machines to further improve asset reliability. 
viii. Mechanisation of track laying activities through use of track machines like 
PQRS, TRT, T-28 etc. 
ix. Interlocking of Level Crossing (LC) Gates for enhancing safety at LC gates. 
x. Use of advanced Phased Array technology of testing of rail and welds. 
xi. Deployment of Integrated Track Monitoring Systems (ITMS) and Oscillation 
Monitoring System (OMS) for comprehensive health assessment to ascertain 
optimal maintenance requirements. 

71 
 
xii. Adoption of portable Track Measuring Trolley for continuous recording of track 
parameters in yards. 
xiii. Using web enabled Track Management System (TMS) for integration and data 
analytics of the track inspection records received through various sources to 
enable precise maintenance inputs.

3. The first field trials on the passenger trains were started in February 2016. Based 
on the experience gained and Independent Safety Assessment of the system by 
Independent Safety Assessor (ISA), three firms were approved in 2018 -19, for 
supply of Kavach Ver 3.2. 
4. Kavach was adopted as National ATP system in July, 2020. 
5. Implementation of Kavach System involves following Key Activities: 
a. Installation of Station Kavach at each and every station, block section. 
b. Installation of RFID Tags throughout the track length. 
c. Installation of telecom Towers throughout the section. 
d. Laying of Optical Fibre Cable along the track.

Railways.

Kavach specification version 4.0 was approved by RDSO on 16.07.2024.

network. This is a significant milestone in safety for Indian Railways. Within a 
short period, IR has developed, tested and started deploying Automatic Train 
Protection System.

Improved Information of Signal Aspects in bigger yards, Station to Station 
Kavach interface on OFC and Direct Interface to existing Electronic Interlocking 
System. With these improvements, Kavach Ver.4.0. is planned for large scale 
deployment over Indian Railways.

15.2 Regarding anticipated cost escalation, major contributing factors and the 
specific measures being undertaken to prevent cost overruns and keep the project 
financially on track and the plan of Indian Railways to fund these cost overruns, the 
Ministry have stated as under : 
“The cost of ₹97,636 crore, approved by CCEA in December, 2015, was based 
on the feasibility report. Detailed engineering review was to be done 
subsequent to the approval of the feasibility report. Construction was initially 
planned partly on viaduct and mostly on embankment. The Empowered 

78 
 
Committee decided to construct entirely on viaduct in 2016 because 
embankment would lead to higher cost of land acquisition; would divide the 
villages; would result in lesser safety because people are likely to trespass; and 
would affect drainage. The cost escalation is thus due to the detailed 
engineering, fluctuation in exchange rate, land, resettlement & Rehabilitation 
cost, normal inflation, costs which were not considered in the feasibility report 
(like utility shifting, power sourcing, station approach development, ticketing, 
Statutory charges etc.) including GST and cess and certain other enabling cost 
to make the corridor operational.  
The major contributory factors are the cost components which were not 
considered in the feasibility report viz. taxes and cess (₹29,330 crore), Utility 
shifting (₹2625 crore), Station approach development (₹2195 crore), Power 
sourcing arrangement (₹1250 crore), Indigenous Rolling Stock and ETCS 
signalling system (₹16,500 crore), ticketing (₹283 crore) and statutory charges 
owing to forest clearances etc (₹400 crore). In addition the escalation due to 
rise in economic factors of production (inflation and price rise) is ₹19,084 crore 
as the project was sanctioned in the year 2015. The substantial increase in land 
rates particularly in urban areas including cost of land at Mumbai, has led to 
the increase in the land, resettlement and rehabilitation cost to ₹16,695 crore.  
The revised cost estimate for the project of Mumbai Ahmedabad High Speed 
Rail Line is under sanction.” 
15.3 Regarding long-term sustainability of high -speed rail operations, roadmap for 
expanding indigenous manufacturing of components under the Make -in-India 
initiative, specific components being indigenised and timelines and institutional 
mechanisms put in place for enhanced domestic capacity development, the Ministry 
have submitted as under : 
“Mumbai- Ahmedabad High Speed Rail project has been a good platform for 
learning, indigenising and executing bullet train projects in the country.  
Make in India Initiative (MII): 

79 
 
Several steps have been taken in indigenising soft and hard skills which 
include: 
1. The principal designer for the project is a Japanese entity. However, the 
design variation during construction have been dealt by Indian agencies, 
duly validated by Centre of Excellences i.e. IITs of the country thereby 
providing a road map and repository of knowledge for dealing with such 
cases in future. The dynamic effect i.e. train -structure interaction 
including deck acceleration, resonance effects (vibration), superstructure 
displacement, train running safety and riding comfort parameters 
increase with train speed and this increase becomes significant at speeds 
greater than 200 kmph i.e. High Speed Railway (HSR). Carrying out 
dynamic analysis for every superstructure span and for different rolling 
stock is an iterative and time -consuming process. Details regarding 
dynamic analysis for HSR, which were not made available by the 
principal designer, have been independently developed (i.e. dynamic 
design charts nomograms) by Indian side for various rolling stocks in 
association with IIT Mumbai. 
2. Similarly in case of Long span steel truss girder designed in Japan and 
fabricated in Indian workshops, performance parameter for Dynamic 
loading has not been shared by the principal Japanese designer. At 
present Indian Railway Standards designs are fit for only 160kmph. To 
ascertain the dynamic performance parameter instrumentations have 
been installed in collaboration with IIT Kanpur, this will help in 
validation of high speed designs parameters through analytical 
modelling and field measurements by the instruments on these girders. 
This will facilitate NHSRCL to finalise design of long span steel truss 
girders for high speed rail in India.       
3. Heavy construction machinery, like moulds, Straddle carrier, bridge 
gantry, girder transporters and launching gantries (all 5 types of 
machines used for full span launching method), which were initially 

80 
 
imported, have been indigenised and are now being manufactured in 
India.  
4. Most of the Track Materials (including track fittings, Insulation pads, 
Reference pins, PC Sleepers, Track Inserts) required for Japanese Slab 
Track Technology has been developed indigenously and being 
manufactured by the Indian Manufactures. Efforts for development of 
Balance 25 % materials are also in process. CAM as per indigenous 
components have been developed in association with IIT Kharagpur and 
same can be adopted after field trials. 
5. Similarly, Track Machineries (like Rail Feeder Car, Track Slab Laying 
Car, Track motor car, Carriage Wagons, CAM Injection Car) required 
for Shinkansen Track technology has been developed and manufactured 
indigenously.  
6. To prevent displacement of girders in the event of an earthquake, each 
girder is provided with 4 number of seismic stoppers. These stoppers, 
made of steel boxed provided with rubberised surfaces, designed for 
High Speed Viaduct, were initially planned to be procured from Japan. 
However, the same have now been indigenously developed and 
manufactured in India for Mumbai- Ahmedabad HSR Project. 
Innovation: 
1. For the first time in the country, a full span launching method has been 
adopted for launching of prestressed box girders weighing around 1000 
MT. The method has been extensively used in the MAHSR project and 
quite unique to the world for this size of launching. The process has been 
highly optimised in terms of quality, safety and speed of construction. A 
girder of 40m length, with this technology, can be launched within 16 
hours.

Training: 
Indian Engineers and Skilled workers (approx. 1000 nos.) have been trained 
for Japanese track methodology and presently, track works are being 
executed under their supervision. A Special Track training facility has been

Stations: 
1. HSR station is not only a transit building but instead is developed as a 
destination or Gateway to the city, hence Station architecture has been 
derived based on some important Characteristics of that city to build 

82 
 
relatability with the local population and to showcase its uniqueness on this 
ambitious project.  
2. The design for Station provides for security measures like controlled entry 
points, baggage scanners, DFMDs (Door Frame Metal Detectors), CCTV 
(Close Circuit Television) cameras etc. 
3. For passenger safety, various architectural features have been used. The 
station roof has been designed leaving sufficient gap above the tracks to 
release the wind pressure created due to passing through trains, crossing the 
station in high speed. As a special safety feature, the false ceiling of the

Geo-technical investigation: 
Greater emphasis has been put on geo technical investigations (GTI) to be 
sure of structural adequacy and to rule out possibility of geological 
surprises. The GTI has been generally carried out at 100 m, and at shorter

Track:

Safety and security:

2. Higher level of security measures has been adopted for operation areas as

3. The design and construction of Civil Engg structures have been carried out

Agency (EPA) Tier 0+ emission standards in HHP Diesel locomotives 
Presently High Horse Power (HHP) Diesel locos do not meet any emission 
norms. In June 2022, Railway Board entrusted RDSO to float EOI for supply of 
Emission kits to upgrade HHP diesel Locomotives to US EPA Tier 0+ emission 
standards. After floating Expression of Interest (EOI), RDSO developed the 
specification for the emission kits for achieving Tier 0+ emission standards.

Original Equipment Manufacturers  (OEMs) of Diesel locomotives viz M/s 
WABTEC and M/s Progress Rail were approached by Northern Railway to 

91 
 
provide a solution for running of Diesel Locomotives in harsh climatic 
conditions of USBRL section. Due to low volumes of the number of 
locomotives to be modified for the new section, both the OEMs didn't provide 
any solution. NR approached RDSO to provide a scheme for modification of 
HHP Diesel locomotives to enable them run in sub zero temp. & high altitudes.

was analysed for suitability to the climate. A scheme for modification was 
developed and provided to NR enabling operation of HHP Diesel locomotives 
over USBRL. Trials were successfully conducted in December 2024 over 
USBRL with WDG4D loco and presently 20 Diesel locomotives are operating 
in USBRL section.

locomotives for provision of Audio Visual indication in Banker/Rear Diesel 
Locomotives for Brake Pipe (BP) pressure drop. This modification in the 
Diesel locomotive will provide additional alert to the loco pilot of the 
Banker/Rear locomotive when Braking is initiated by the loco pilot of the 
leading locomotive so that the loco pilot in Banker/rear loco can also initiate 
braking simultaneously. This enhances the safety of train operation in Ghat 
section of Railways.

17.1 The Ministry detailed the following policy measures, infrastructure upgrades 
and operational strategies  being implemented/ proposed to be implemented by Indian 
Railways to achieve Net Zero Carbon Emissions by 2030 : 
Indian Railways (IR) is an environment friendly means of bulk transportation system 
and it has set a target of making itself 'Net Zero Carbon Emitter' (NZCE) by 2030. A 
number of initiatives are being taken by Indian Railways in the area of green 
technology and sustainable practices. Expansion and modernization works are taking 
place over IR in which environment related aspects are taken care of and provision 
of funds for the same is provided. Additionally, provision for Environment Related 
Works (ERW) fund has been made an integral part of work estimates of certain plan 
heads, which is 0.5% of the total amount sanctioned under that Plan Head. Apart 
from that, Indian Railways has taken following key measures to promote renewable 
energy, sustainable and green practices: 
1. Establishment of dedicated wing for Environment related affairs: Ministry of 
Railways has set up Environment and Housekeeping Management (EnHM) 
Directorate in Railway Board in year 2015 to deal with the issues related to 
Environment as well as Housekeeping Management of Indian Railways. EnHM 
wings are also established in all Zones. 
2. Electrification: Indian Railways has electrified about 99.4% of the total broad -
gauge network of Indian Railways. The electrification in remaining network has 
been taken up. Electrification carried out during 2014 -25 & before 2014 is as 
under:  

100

Before 2014 (about 60 years)  21,801 
2014-25 46,900 
 
 
3. Solar & Wind Energy installed over Indian Railways: Increasing use of 
renewable energy sources, such as solar and wind power, across railway 
operations to improve overall energy efficiency and sustainability. Till January 
2026, about 1092 Mega Watt (MW) of solar power plant (both rooftop and land) 
and around 103 Mega Watt (MW) of wind power plants have been 
commissioned over Indian Railways. In addition, 100 MW of renewable power 
under Round the Clock (RTC) mode has also started flowing. 
4. Energy Efficiency Measures: 
• Introduction of Insulated -Gate Bipolar Transistor (IGBT) based 3 -phase 
propulsion system with regenerative braking in Electrical Multiple Unit 
(EMU) trains, Mainline Electrical Multiple Unit (MEMU) trains, Kolkata 
Metro rakes and Namo Bharat Rapid Rail (Vande Metro) to conserve energy 
during the operations. 
• All new passenger electric locomotives are being manufactured with Hotel 
Load converter to feed Hotel load supply to LHB coaches leading to saving in 
diesel besides being energy efficient. Also, conversion of existing End on 
Generation (EOG) trains into Head On Generation (HOG) trains to reduce 
noise and air pollution at stations and in trains.  
• Energy saving mode on three -phase locomotives has been provided on three - 
phase electric locomotives to reduce power consumption during stationary 
conditions. 
• Loco Pilots are trained during their initial training as well as during 
promotional training and refresher courses for saving of energy/fuel to 
achieve better energy/fuel efficiency by good driving technique, good road 

101 
 
learning and simulator training. Loco Pilots are being regularly counselled to 
use of coasting, regenerative braking feature and switch off blowers in case 
detention is more than 15 minutes to save energy. 
• Trailing locomotives of Multi Units (MU) hauling light loads are switched off 
to save energy. 
• Provision of external 750V power supply at washing/sick lines for 
maintenance and testing of LHB coaches. 
• Provision of energy efficient Light Emitting Diode (LED) lighting in Railway 
installations including Railway stations, service buildings, coaches, 
EMUs/MEMUs for reduction in electricity consumption.  
• Use of automatic platform lighting management system at stations as per train 
services/passenger requirement. 
• Use of timer on high mast tower lightings/street lighting/circulating area of 
Railway stations. 
• Use of energy efficient Brushless Direct Current (BLDC) motor fans in 
coaches and buildings. 
• Use of capacitor banks in traction sub -stations to maintain near unity power 
factor for energy saving. 
• Procurement of BEE 5 -Star rated appliances, Variable Frequency Drives 
(VFDs), energy efficient motors and pumps.  
5. Environment Management Plan: Redevelopment of Railway Stations: In 
redevelopment process, all environmental norms are duly considered for 
achieving sustainable modernization of stations. A specific committee of officers 
has been constituted to grant the clearance for the Environment Management 
Plan(EMP) of station redevelopment projects. All aspects of Environment 
Protection (EP Acts) are being taken care of during the process of sanction of 
EMP, which are broadly enumerated below:- 
a. Adherence to the stipulations made / observed by the State Pollution 
Control Board and the State Government. 
b. Statutory compliance; 
c. Air quality monitoring and preservation; 

102 
 
d. Water quality monitoring and preservatin;  
e. Noise monitoring and prevention; 
f. Energy Conservation measures; Waste Management; 
g. Green Cover; 
 
6. Green Rating/Certification: IR has taken the initiative of undertaking Green 
Rating Certification for different types of Railway establishments, including the 
industrial units. Such certification mainly covers assessment of parameters 
having direct bearing on environment, such as, energy conservation measures, 
use of renewable energy, impact on GHG emission, water conservation, solid and
